calls.reason: The only instance is one UBS analyst asking at SAP's Q2 call whether token costs sit in R&D. It came in what SAP called a strong quarter with 24% cloud growth, so it is a thin case of investors questioning token-driven R&D.

Reporting by Ars Technica, the FT and CNBC shows a $20.9B operating loss and about $8B cash burn on $13.1B of 2025 revenue. The reported $300B, five-year Oracle deal works out to about $60B a year, far above that revenue.
Nothing shows Microsoft can't afford compute subsidies. Its FY2026 results show $133.7B net income, so the condition the claim depends on never happened.
No inventory links data centers under construction to their end customers, so the 50% share can't be checked. Meta's $21B CoreWeave deal shows some outside demand but doesn't settle the hedged claim.

No Stargate project accounts or payment records are available. At Investor Day, Oracle only called infrastructure a lower-margin, capital-intensive business, which can't show when the projects turn a profit.
The forecast has no deadline. As of late October 2026, Anthropic had filed for an IPO and Kiplinger read the market as late cycle, not a confirmed peak; no industry collapse has happened.
